identity: An Arabic Wikipedia encyclopedia article on الفلسفة (Philosophy), evidently translated from the English Wikipedia lead and history sections. Formal MSA, third-person expository register, no narration and no dialogue. Its physical structure is: (1) a two-paragraph lead defining philosophy and sketching its historical scope; (2) bare section headings sitting alone on their own lines (مقدمة / المعرفة / التقدم الفلسفي / تاريخ الفلسفة / الفلسفة الغربية / فلسفة الشرق الأوسط), each flanked by <NL>; (3) body paragraphs of survey prose dense with proper names, century labels, bare date pairs (parenthetical life-dates stripped of their brackets, e.g. 570 495 قبل الميلاد, 1596 1650, 980 يونيو 1037) and long coordinated enumerations of disciplines and thinkers; (4) a three-item bulleted list at indices 391-441 giving the classical tripartite division of philosophy, each bullet occupying its own <NL>-delimited line; (5) short runs of rhetorical questions used as examples of philosophical problems (indices 62-72, 80-107, 216-241).
law: The sentence unit is the single finite predication: one verb-initial (VSO) clause, or one topic-comment nominal clause, together with everything that hangs off it (relative clauses with الذي/التي/والتي, adjuncts, appositive glosses, and مثل/بما في ذلك enumerations). A boundary falls where a NEW finite predication begins with no syntactic tie back to the preceding one. The reliable positive triggers here are: (a) a bare finite verb starting a fresh clause after an already-complete clause (تشمل، شملت، أصبحت، انقسمت، ولدت، شهدت، نوقشت، طور، تعرضت، يدعي، يمكن، كان); (b) a fronted adverbial or PP opening a new predication (على سبيل المثال، في القرن التاسع عشر، في العصر الحديث، في الجزء الأول من...، في مصر القديمة، في وقت لاحق، بعد الفتوحات الإسلامية، مع صعود الإمبراطورية، على النقيض من ذلك، تاريخيا، تقليديا، بمعنى عام، لقد); (c) a definite topic NP opening a nominal sentence after a complete clause (التقاليد الأخرى، الفلاسفة المعاصرون، بعض المفكرين، هذا التقسيم، التيارات الرئيسية، البعض الآخر، أدب الحكمة، الفلسفة اليهودية); (d) the end of each rhetorical question in a question run, since each carried its own question mark before punctuation was stripped. The reliable negative triggers are: subordinators, which never start a new sentence (بينما، حيث، لأنه، الذي/التي/والتي/الذين، ما قبل), and و/ف used as plain coordination inside one predication (وتعود، وأصر، وهيمنت، وتشمل، وكان يطلق). The genuinely ambiguous class is و + a discourse-anaphoric adverbial (وبهذا المعنى) or و + a past verb whose subject and topic both switch (وشملت الموضوعات): Arabic encyclopedic prose habitually opens a new sentence with و, so these are scored as boundaries but only at medium confidence. Headings are their own sentence unit by fiat of the <NL> rule. Bare date pairs, transliterated Greek/Egyptian glosses (φιλοσοφία, philosophia, physis, physiologoi, sebayt) and appositive gloss NPs (التعاليم، الشعارات، اللاهوت القديم) are stripped parentheses, not clause breaks, and never take a boundary of their own.
reasoning: HARD SITE 1, index 114 (المعرفة). The string reads تاريخيا الفلسفة تشمل أي مجموعة من المعرفة من وقت ... أرسطو إلى القرن التاسع عشر شملت الفلسفة الطبيعية علم الفلك. Two finite verbs (تشمل, شملت) sit here with no connector, so a break is forced. The only question is where the من وقت ... إلى القرن التاسع عشر span attaches. It cannot be a complement of تشمل (which already has its object أي مجموعة من المعرفة), and شملت is left subjectless-fronted without it; the from-X-to-Y frame is the classic fronted temporal adjunct of the second clause. Boundary at 114, not at 124. HIGH. HARD SITE 2, the three question runs (68, 72 / 85, 102, 107 / 220, 230, 241). These are enumerated philosophical questions each introduced by هل or ما, each of which carried a terminal question mark in the source. I treat every question as its own sentence. The run-internal ones (68, 85, 102, 220, 230) get MED because they follow a colon-introduced list and I cannot verify from the stripped text that each closed with a mark rather than a comma; the run-final ones (72, 107, 241) get HIGH because a plainly new predication follows regardless (يطرح الفلاسفة / تاريخيا الفلسفة / الحقول الفرعية الرئيسية). I deliberately do NOT place a boundary at 61 (الكلاسيكية) or at 215 (المثال): those are colon positions introducing the list, and a colon is not a sentence terminator. HARD SITE 3, index 547 (العلوم) - REJECTED. ...يرى ديفيد تشالمرز وغيرهم تقدما في الفلسفة مشابها للتقدم في العلوم بينما قال تالبوت بروير إن التقدم هو المعيار الخاطئ. بينما is a subordinating conjunction; the قال-clause is a dependent contrastive adjunct of the يرى-clause. No boundary. The whole contrast pair is one sentence running 533-563. HARD SITE 4, the وبهذا المعنى sites, 283 and 577. Both are formally coordinable: يشير ... وبهذا المعنى ترتبط, and ترتبط ... وبهذا المعنى تطرح. But بهذا المعنى is a discourse-level anaphor resuming the whole preceding assertion, which is a sentence-opening move, not a within-clause one, and Arabic encyclopedic prose routinely opens sentences with و. Scored as boundaries at MED. HARD SITE 5, index 745 (وأبيقورية). التقاليد الأخرى تشمل ... وأبيقورية وشملت الموضوعات المهمة التي غطاها الإغريق الميتافيزيقيا. The و here is followed by a past-tense VSO clause with a wholly new subject, after a present-tense nominal clause; reading it as coordination would make أبيقورية and الموضوعات المهمة co-objects, which is incoherent. Boundary, MED for the residual و-doubt. HARD SITE 6, indices 463 and 484 (ولدت). These look و-initial but are not: ولدت is the finite verb walada/wullidat governing الفلسفة الأخلاقية / الفلسفة الميتافيزيقية. Bare verb-initial clauses, HIGH. HARD SITE 7, indices 441 and 447. The third list bullet is not closed by an <NL>; the prose هذا التقسيم ليس قديما ولكنه تغير and everything after it continues on the same line. So 441 (الأخرى) and 447 (تغير) are ordinary internal boundaries that must be supplied by hand, even though the parallel first two bullets got theirs free from the <NL> rule at 408 and 426. HARD SITE 8, the long enumeration sentences at 617-667, 954-995 and 787-817. Each contains many appositions and relative clauses (الذي أسس، الذي طور، شخصية رئيسية في المثالية الألمانية، المعاداة للمسيحية) that in the source were comma- or semicolon-separated list items inside one sentence. I place NO boundaries inside them: the list items are not finite independent predications, they are appositive glosses on names. HARD SITE 9, index 1142 (والإسلامية). شارك المفكرون اليهود ... مع الفلسفة اليونانية والإسلامية في وقت لاحق تعرضت الفلسفة اليهودية. Two finite verbs, no connector, so a break is forced; في وقت لاحق reads as Later opening the second clause rather than as a temporal tail on شارك. Boundary at 1142, HIGH. MANDATORY SITES. The token before each of the 21 <NL> tokens (194, 270, 272, 274, 390, 409, 427, 504, 507, 564, 567, 613, 616, 704, 786, 907, 1016, 1020, 1167, 1195, 1291) and the final token 1331 are boundaries by rule: 193, 269, 271, 273, 389, 408, 426, 503, 506, 563, 566, 612, 615, 703, 785, 906, 1015, 1019, 1166, 1194, 1290, 1331. Note 271 (مقدمة) and 273 (المعرفة) are one-word headings that are therefore one-word sentences, and 786 is a paragraph break that does NOT introduce a standalone heading - فلسفة العصور الوسطى القرنين الخامس والسادس عشر هي الفترة... is running prose, so no boundary is placed at 789. TOTAL: 81 sentences over 1311 non-<NL> tokens, mean ~16 tokens per sentence, which matches the density of MSA encyclopedic prose.
